statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-134703: the DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 conversion functions in xmltok.c in libexpat through 2.10.0 can split a valid surrogate pair when output space is limited, so an XML_UNICODE build parsing UTF-16 input in non-native byte order can hand isolated high surrogates to character data and default handlers (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-134703). Upstream fixed it in libexpat pull request #1519 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/pull/1519), commit 702389c (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/commit/702389c818cb402f2423fa998fa11907d621959f), with commit 81e0738 making the explicit-endianness UTF-16 decoders accessible. It is released in Expat 2.11.0 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/R_2_11_0/expat/Changes), and Debian lists only unstable's 2.11.0-1 as fixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-134703). The code is compiled into this owner's library; DHI backported both commits to expat 2.10.0 for Alpine 3.23 in build 2.10.0-r2. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes expat builds 2.7.3-r0, 2.7.4-r0, 2.7.5-r0, 2.8.1-r0, 2.8.2-r0, 2.8.3-r0, 2.8.3-r1, 2.8.4-r0, 2.8.5-r0, 2.8.5-r1, 2.9.0-r1, 2.10.0-r1 and 2.10.0-r2, and every build before 2.10.0-r2 was published before the upstream fix was written. On x86_64 and aarch64, libexpat.a in the expat-static package of 2.10.0-r2 contains the XmlGetUtf16LittleEndianEncoding function added by that pull request, and libexpat.a of 2.10.0-r1 does not. The request also matches 2.9.0-r0, which the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository does not publish and which sorts below the boundary. The range ends at 2.10.0-r2, the first published build with the fix.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-134703: in libexpat 2.10.0 and earlier, the UTF-16 to UTF-16 conversion functions in xmltok.c (DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16) can split a valid surrogate pair when output space is short, so a crafted document in non-native byte order UTF-16 can deliver a lone high surrogate to the character data and default handlers (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-134703, https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/pull/1519). Only builds compiled with XML_UNICODE convert parser input with those functions; a UTF-8 build converts with XmlUtf8Convert instead (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/R_2_9_0/expat/lib/xmlparse.c). Upstream fixed it after the 2.10.0 release in https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/commit/702389c818cb402f2423fa998fa11907d621959f, which no expat release contains yet, and Debian lists trixie's 2.9.0-1~deb13u1 as vulnerable. The DHI expat packages for Debian 13 are built from Debian's expat 2.7.1, 2.8.2, 2.8.3 and 2.9.0 sources. We unpacked every published build for amd64 and arm64: each libexpat1 package ships both libexpat.so.1, a UTF-8 build, and libexpatw.so.1, an XML_UNICODE build (its feature list names XML_UNICODE, which libexpat.so.1 does not), and each libexpat1-dev package ships the matching static libexpat.a and libexpatw.a. None of these builds carries the fix, so applications that use libexpatw are affected; libexpat.so.1 and the xmlwf program built on it convert input to UTF-8 and do not use the affected functions.
